title: Ang 524–526: Gujri's Bhagats
hookLine: Kabir, Namdev, Ravidas, Trilochan and Jaidev
tomorrow: which street do you take to find someone you love?

lines: A GIFT FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS IT ALL.
cards: Shopping for someone who already has everything is its own small panic. Ravidas has that problem with God, on ang 525. The milk?
The calf got to it first. The flower? A bee's been in it.
Even the water has been swum through by fish. So what's left to offer?

teach.b: His answer, in paraphrase: I offer my body and mind in worship, and by the Guru's grace I find the Pure One. One more line from the same hymn: snakes coil around the sandalwood tree; poison and nectar live together.
Even the sandalwood has company. Ravidas is one of five Bhagats who close Gujri, side by side.

Kabir, whose mother weeps that her son has left the loom; how will the children eat? Namdev: give me a kingdom, and what glory is that; send me begging, and what have I lost? Ravidas and his offering.
Trilochan, on what the mind holds at its very last moment. And Jaidev.
Five voices sharing the last pages of one raga.
And that's this week in one picture, too. Look back. Sandalwood.
From the heart. Gujri begins, with the mind as the stone. The Gurus in Gujri, and food inside the rock.
The third's ballad and the narrow gate. The fifth's ballad, all of you turned one way. Six lines.
The games are bringing them back.

how: Sikhs reading the Granth in order reach the Bhagats' hymns at the end of Gujri, after the Gurus' hymns and vars; Ravidas's hymn of the offering is sung in kirtan like the rest.

o: where the five Bhagats' hymns in Gujri begin
where Guru Arjan's ballad in Gujri ends
where Farid's hymns in the raga of Asa begin

p: his mother weeps over the loom
the calf drank the milk first
the mind at its last moment

s: Ravidas says he has nothing worth offering, so he gives up
he offers his body and mind, and by the Guru's grace finds the Pure One.
Gujri's Bhagats include Trilochan and Jaidev
with Kabir, Namdev and Ravidas: five voices close the raga.
Ravidas's hymn pictures snakes around a sandalwood tree
poison and nectar, he says, live together.

games.q: it's your grandmother's birthday. your cousins bought gifts; you're broke this month. what fits Ravidas on ang 525?
o: give her an afternoon: sit with her, cook with her, listen.
skip the visit; with nothing to give, it's better to stay away.
borrow money; a bought gift is what makes the offering real.
games.why: Ravidas finds every gift already used: milk, flower, water. so he offers what's left, his body and mind. yourself is the gift.

practice: Count on your fingers six things from this week that someone else got to before you: a meal cooked, a ride, a message, a laugh. Then rest your hands palms up for the sit, offering what's left, the way Ravidas does.
If you'd like, read ang 526 first, where Trilochan and Jaidev close the raga.

wordCard.voice: Ang 524. Where Gujri's Bhagats begin: Kabir first, then Namdev, Ravidas, Trilochan and Jaidev.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: tan man, body and mind, what Ravidas offers in worship (ang 525).

carryVoice: Five Bhagats, one raga, and an offering that was only ever yourself. See you next week.
